title: Interval overlap test — Time-Interval Search
description: Two intervals overlap unless one ends before the other begins: NOT (e1 < s2 OR e2 < s1). This single test answers 'did these events coincide' in constant time. Overlap is the primitive behind every temporal query.
demo:
# Time-interval search: Allen-style overlap test over event intervals.
from datetime import date
events = {k: (date.fromisoformat(a), date.fromisoformat(b)) for k, (a, b) in {'a': ('2024-03-10', '2024-03-12'), 'b': ('2024-02-20', '2024-03-05'), 'c': ('2024-04-01', '2024-04-02')}.items()}
qs, qe = date.fromisoformat("2024-03-01"), date.fromisoformat("2024-03-31")
def relation(s, e):
    if e < qs or s > qe: return "disjoint"
    if s >= qs and e <= qe: return "during"
    if s < qs and e > qe: return "contains"
    if s < qs: return "overlaps-start"
    return "overlaps-end"
print(f"Query window: {qs} to {qe}")
for name, (s, e) in events.items():
    r = relation(s, e)
    if r != "disjoint":
        print(f"  {name}: {s}..{e} ({r})")
provenance: Public methodology — standard computer-science technique documented in the technical literature; fact-checked 2026-10-21.
